title: Does a review by a second model find method-level problems the reader panel misses?
hypothesis: With the same reading copy and the same prompt, a model from a different vendor finds method-level problems in a full draft that a same-family reader panel does not. If so, DR-011's cross-vendor Pass 3 may belong before a full draft goes to an outside reader.
subject: DR-011 Pass 3 (cross-vendor review) against the reader panel, same prompt (agents/review-prompt.md)
judge: the paper's author, blind to which arm raised each finding

population.note: the next full draft of one private narrative review

decision_rationale: Preregistered before the draft is reviewed; no result yet. Bars, counting rules and the mapping to a decision are in the PREREGISTRATION.md.
notes: The draft and both reviews are private. The concluding entry's metrics will trace to an anonymised summary, so for a reader without the private files the metric check is circular (DR-024 rule 6).

title: Does the framework's rule set, used as a reviewer prompt, find more planted faults than a competent plain review prompt?
hypothesis: Prompted with the framework rules (Step Z tiers, grounds/warrant, normative boundary conditions, calculation recompute, scope drift, contribution check), a text-only reviewer finds more planted faults in a sourced essay than with a plain prompt naming the usual categories, at no loss of precision. If so, the rule prompt earns its place as the DR-011 blind pass.
subject: the framework rule set as a text-only reviewer prompt (DR-011 blind-pass use), against a plain category-naming prompt; not the registry + source-check process
judge: Claude (also the seeder), scoring on shuffled ids against a preregistered answer key; blinding partial (framework outputs recognisable by wording)

population.note: 2 arms x 2 reviewers x 2 repetitions on a seeded copy of one third-party essay; 2 extra plain runs on the original for native-issue recall; plus the 2 framework-prompt runs on the original from 2026-11-14 (runs_original_prior)

decision_rationale: Rejected for the blind-pass use only, by the preregistered rule: H1 failed (16 vs 16) and H3 was violated by 12.2 points, mostly one false-positive pattern traced to rule 4. Caveat: the primary comparison hit a ceiling (too-blatant seeding), so a v2 with harder faults and a process arm decides; if it reverses this, a new entry corrects this one. The framework's process claim (registry + source checks) was not tested.
notes: Pilot, n = 4 per arm. Preregistration written before the runs but kept off-repo and committed afterwards (DR-024 rule 1 deviation; timeline and SHA-256 in SUMMARY.md). Essay, seeded copy and raw outputs quote a third-party essay (anonymised in the evidence) and stay off-repo; metrics trace to scores.tsv and SUMMARY.md here, whose underlying outputs are private, so the metric check is partly circular (DR-024 rule 6 by analogy). On source-fault detection the model effect (Codex vs Vibe) exceeded the prompt effect; on findings count and precision it did not. spend_usd null: subscription plans, not metered.
